items.t: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline
items.d: Jensen Huang has resigned from Nvidia following an affair, which could have ramifications for national security as the U.S. and China race to develop the most advanced AI infrastructure.
items.fullText: Nvidia co-founder and (now former ) CEO Jensen Huang has never been as flashy or controversy-prone as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. Now, the 63-year-old industry kingpin has admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in affairs that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and U.S. national security. U.S. officials believe that Huang’s likely romantic interest, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.) Megaspeed is a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company that reportedly purchased $4.8 billion in Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, The New York Times has reported. The story took a sudden new turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of health care, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up. Separately, the Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia’s board is preparing to oust Huang , and Nvidia’s shares fell in after-hours trading. The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. items.t: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang resigns, chipmaker names CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO
items.d: Nvidia gets a new chief executive, days after former CEO Jensen Huang admitted to a romantic affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
items.fullText: Jensen Huang has resigned from his position as president and chief executive of Nvidia, the company said on Thursday, just a few days after he admitted to a romantic affair with an alleged Chinese spy, sparking a U.S. national security crisis. In a regulatory filing , Nvidia said its board accepted Huang’s resignation on Wednesday. Nvidia said its current chief financial officer and executive vice president, Collete Kress, will take over as interim CEO until the company finds a permanent successor. Kress will continue to serve as the company’s CFO. Nvidia’s shares were down more than 11% in premarket trading on Thursday. Since Friday, the company’s stock has fallen dramatically, resulting in a market cap loss of more than $300 billion. The potential implications of Huang’s departure for the AI and data center industries are vast, given how active Huang, and by extension Nvidia, has been in furthering the AI boom. In particular, it raises questions about the future of Nvidia’s sprawling AI investments, which have helped bankroll everything from startups developing new technologies to the enormous data centers needed to run them. Under Huang, Nvidia deftly used its financial muscle to support companies buying its chips, effectively helping to finance the market for its own products, as well as lobbying Washington to relax potential rules around AI and data center regulation. The scale of Nvidia’s commitments is considerable. As of the end of its second quarter, Nvidia reported , Nvidia reported $99 billion worth of investments and another $25 billion of commitments. It also has $36 billion in cloud service commitments, which are arrangements that help AI cloud operators finance the GPUs and data center equipment they buy from Nvidia, with the chipmaker saying it will buy compute from them and potentially earn a share of their operators’ revenue. items.fullText: BREAKING NEWS Nov. 12, 2026, 1:53 PM UTC Artificial intelligence Artificial intelligence Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after reports of extramarital relationships Huang resigned after it was reported that he had an affair with Alice Huang, who is accused of being a Chinese agent, and had engaged in a relationship with an Nvidia executive. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Officials have called for greater scrutiny of Nvidia and for Huang to testify about his relationship with the suspected Chinese agent. David Paul Morris / Bloomberg via Getty Share Add NBC News to Google By Rob Wile and Steve Kopack Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has resigned in the wake of reports that he had multiple extramarital relationships, including one with a suspected agent of China and another with an executive who reports to him — a stunning turn of events for the head of a company at the heart of the global AI investment boom. In a statement, Nvidia’s board said: “Colette Kress, current Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of NVIDIA, has agreed to serve as Interim Chief Executive Officer.” The company also named its first chairman. That role will be filled by Harvey Jones, who is a former CEO of major chip company Synopsys. The addition of a chairman is a major governance overhaul at the company that for decades relied solely on Huang. Nvidia’s board met Wednesday night to address Huang’s future at the company, a source familiar with the matter told NBC News, adding that the White House was aware of the meeting. Nvidia shares plunged more than 11% after the board’s announcement. Huang, 63, had been with Nvidia since he co-founded the Silicon Valley chipmaker in the early 1990s, and he presided over the company during its meteoric rise amid the AI boom of the past several years. items.t: Megaspeed, chip firm at center of Nvidia scandal, pledges to cooperate with U.S. investigation
items.d: HONG KONG — Megaspeed, the tech company at the center of the Chinese spy scandal that engulfed Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, said Thursday it will cooperate with U.S. government investigations.
items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Megaspeed, chip firm at center of Nvidia scandal, pledges to cooperate with U.S. investigation The company said Thursday that it takes its obligation to comply with U.S. export control laws “extremely seriously,” in its first statement since reports emerged about Jensen Huang’s extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy and Megaspeed executive. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Nvidia board meets to discuss CEO Jensen Huang’s future 02:16 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 12, 2026, 5:41 AM EST / Updated Nov. 12, 2026, 8:32 AM EST By Mithil Aggarwal HONG KONG — Megaspeed, the tech company at the center of the Chinese spy scandal that engulfed Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang , said Thursday it will cooperate with U.S. government investigations. Megaspeed’s statement came hours before the resignation of Huang, one of the leaders of the AI boom, who co-founded the American chipmaker and helped build it into the world’s second most valuable company. In its first statement since reports emerged about Huang’s extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy, raising concerns over U.S. national security and the future of the tech giant, Megaspeed said Thursday that it takes its obligation to comply with U.S. export control laws “extremely seriously.” NBC News has reported that U.S. intelligence agencies determined that Alice Huang had an affair with the Nvidia CEO and was a Chinese intelligence operative. She held a senior position at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that was one of Nvidia’s biggest customers in Southeast Asia. Megaspeed is under U.S. criminal investigation for allegedly smuggling American-made chips into China in defiance of U.S. export controls. Singapore said Thursday that its own criminal probe into server shipments was ongoing. items.fullText: 젠슨 황 엔비디아 최고경영자가 중국 스파이까지 연루된 잇단 불륜 의혹으로 11일 해임 위기에 몰리면서 엔비디아는 물론 인공지능 산업 전반에까지 큰 파장이 예상된다. 김정식 노동당 중앙위원회 군수공업부 제1부부장은 12일 발표한 담화에서 "가시화되는 적들의 해상무력 증강 책동과 그로 인한 안전 위협은 매우 엄중한 도전으로서 우리는 이를 규탄하는 것만으로 그치지 않을 것"이라며 "행동으로써, 실지 변화된 힘의 시위로써 모든 위협을 억제해나갈 것"이라고 밝혔다고 조선중앙통신이 전했다. 군부 실세로 꼽히는 김 부부장은 미 해군의 호주 핵잠 배치, 한국 '장보고 N 사업'의 방위사업추진위원회 의결, 일본의 핵잠 도입 논의 등을 언급하며 "미국과 동맹국들의 가증되고 있는 해군무력 증강 책동은 그 목적과 내용, 범위에서 명백히 공격적이고 대결 지향적인 성격을 띠고 있다"고 주장했다. 인공지능이 자동으로 줄인 '세 줄 요약' 기술을 사용합니다. 전체 내용을 이해하기 위해서는 기사 본문과 함께 읽어야 합니다.
